[text-2] heading "Chocolate Chip Cookie recipe"
[text-3] "A long awaited reader request…. I’ve lost count of the number of times I’ve had people writing in asking for my chocolate chip cookie recipe!"
[text-4] "In truth, I was sitting on it because I wanted to make sure I tested it properly for different measures in different countries. If you’ve ever tried a cookie recipe written by someone in another country and had it fail miserably, chances are that it’s because of the difference in cup, tablespoon and"
[text-5] "For most recipes, the difference between measures is not enough to affect the recipe or the difference is proportional across the whole recipe so it still works fine. However, for baking recipes, you really have to be careful. Especially cookies and cakes."
[text-6] "So that’s a little tip for you when using baking recipes – check the country of origin of the writer. If it’s not your country, proceed with caution! 😉"
[text-7] "Oh – in case I forgot to make it really clear – yes I’ve tested this recipe using Australian & rest of world cups (all exc US are very similar) and US cups and weight measures."
[text-8] "Oh – and this is based on a Cooks’ Illustrated tried and tested recipe. That always helps!"
[text-9] "This chocolate chip cookie recipe may be a little different to most you’ve come across. It’s unique in that there’s no creaming butter, no electric beater is required, there’s no refrigeration of the dough (unless it’s stinking hot where you are!) and there’s no rolling dough."
[text-10] "Dump and mix. The batter will be quite soft at first because of the melted butter, but after 5 minutes or so, it firms up into a soft dough that can be scooped onto the baking tray and it holds its form perfectly. Using an ice cream scooper with a lever (seriously handy kitchen utensil – cookies, pa"
[text-11] "I’ve tried to capture how soft these cookies are in the recipe video (below the recipe). I hope I’ve succeeded. I also hope I’ve succeeded in showing you how straight forward these are to make."
[text-12] "Dangerous. I should have called these Dangerous Choc Chip Cookies."
[text-13] "Happy weekend everyone! – Nagi xx"

[text-30] "RECIPE VIDEO ABOVE. This is my I need chocolate chip cookies now recipe that makes soft, buttery cookies. No waiting for butter to soften, no electric beater, no refrigeration time, no rolling dough into balls. The hardest part is waiting for them to cool!"
[text-31] "Adapted from Cooks Illustrated. Makes 13 large or 26-30 small. {This recipe will work no matter which country you live in – see Note 5. High altitude baking – see Note 6.}"
[text-32] "Note: For my Rolls Royce Chocolate Chip Cookies, see here (it requires overnight refrigeration and worth the wait!)."
[text-33] heading "Ingredients"
[text-34] list item "▢ 1 3/4 cups plain / all purpose flour"
[text-35] list item "▢ 1 tsp salt"
[text-36] list item "▢ ½ tsp baking soda (bi carb soda)"
[text-37] list item "▢ 175g / 12 tbsp unsalted butter , cut into 2 cm/ 4/5″ cubes (1.5 US sticks / 6 oz)"
[text-38] list item "▢ 1/2 cup brown sugar , packed (light or dark) (Note 1)"
[text-39] list item "▢ 1/2 cup caster sugar (US: granulated sugar)"
[text-40] list item "▢ 1 egg"
[text-41] list item "▢ 1 egg yolk"
[text-42] list item "▢ 2 tsp vanilla extract"
[text-43] list item "▢ 1 1/4 cups chocolate chips , separated (US: semi sweet chocolate chips or chunks)"
[text-44] heading "Instructions"
[text-45] list item "Preheat oven to 180C / 350F (standard) or 160C/320F (fan / convection). Place oven shelf in the middle of the oven."
[text-46] list item "Line 2 trays with baking / parchment paper."
[text-47] list item "Whisk the flour, salt and baking soda in a bowl."
[text-48] list item "Place the butter in a large heatproof bowl. Microwave until the butter is almost fully melted (25 sec for room temp butter, 40 sec for fridge cold butter on high)."
[text-49] list item "Whisk to finish melting the butter. (Note 2)"
[text-50] list item "Add brown and white sugar, whisk energetically for 15 seconds."
[text-51] list item "Add egg, yolk and vanilla, whisk well for 15 seconds."
[text-52] list item "Add flour mixture and mix until flour is almost fully incorporated."
[text-53] list item "Add 1 cup chocolate chips, stir to disperse and flour is fully incorporated. Batter will be quite loose."
[text-54] list item "Stand for 5 minutes for batter to firm up a bit so it is scoop-able into mounds. (Note 3)"
[text-55] list item "LARGE COOKIES: Scoop up a level ice cream scoop / 3 tbsp / 1/4 cup (Note 4) and place on baking trays 5cm / 2″ apart – 13 balls. Top with remaining choc chips (these remain on surface once baked = prettier)."
[text-56] list item "SMALL COOKIES (26 – 30): Scoop up 1.5 tbsp (heaped tbsp measure) OR 1/2 an ice cream scoop (this works well). Place on baking trays 4cm / 1.75″ apart, top with choc chops."
[text-57] list item "Bake 1 tray at a time. LARGE COOKIES: Bake for 8 minutes, then rotate the tray and bake for 3 minutes (11 minutes in total). SMALL COOKIES: Bake 6 minutes, turn then bake 3 minutes (9 min total). The cookies should be just golden on the edges and pale golden on top. They will be slightly puffed up."
[text-58] list item "Cool on the tray – they finish cooking. They will lose the puffiness while resting. Dig in and get your cookie fix!"
[text-59] heading "Recipe Notes:"
[text-60] "1. I switch between light and dark brown sugar, I use whatever I have. If I had both, I probably use light over dark more often. The flavour difference is not noticeable to me. Light brown sugar will produce a slightly paler cookie which does suggest its softness."
[text-61] "2. If the butter is fully melted in the microwave so it’s transparent when you take it out, the cookie is not quite as soft. Not a deal breaker, just a little tip that makes a difference!"
[text-62] "3. FIRMING UP BATTER: While the butter is warm, the batter is quite loose (see video). Standing for just 5 minutes firms up the batter, turning it into a soft cookie dough so when you drop mounds onto the tray, they stay in a mound shape. If it is super hot where you are, you may need to refrigerate"
[text-63] "4. A standard ice cream scooper is 3 tablespoons. The ones with levers like what I use in the video are a terrific utensil that I use more frequently for things like cookies, pancakes and even meatballs more than I do ice cream!"
[text-64] "You can also make smaller cookies and I will update this recipe with a guide for baking times for different size cookies in the near future – there are cookie baking plans for this weekend!"
[text-65] "5. HIGH ALTITUDE BAKING – a reader at 7200 ft reported that this worked perfectly with the sugar reduced to 3/4 cup (total)."
[text-66] "DIFFERENT COUNTRY CUPS: No need to do any calculations to adjust, this recipe will work no matter which country you are in with the exception of Japan, please use weights provided."
[text-67] "Background: Measuring cups and teaspoons can differ between some countries. For most recipes, the difference is not material enough to affect the recipe. However, for baking recipes, it does make a difference. I’ve tested this recipe with US cups, Aussie cups (which is very close to rest of world) a"
[text-68] "6. STORING: Keeps great for 3 days in an airtight container and they freeze well too. Dough keeps great in the fridge for 3 days – it will firm up so roll into balls and place on tray, then add 1 minutes to the bake time. Cooked cookies freeze great – defrost before serving."
[text-69] "7. HIGH ALTITUDE BAKING: I’m thrilled to share that a reader, Marg (4 June 2017) who lives at high altitude (985 m/3200 ft) made the following adjustments: reduced total sugar to 1/2 cup (1/4 each brown and white), increased oven to 170C/340F, and used 2 eggs (to avoid having left over egg white). S"
[text-70] "The Cooks’ Illustrated recipe I adapted my recipe from doesn’t prescribe exact adjustments, but provided a guideline which Marg based her adjustments on: “For High-Altitude Baking: Problem: Cookies spread too much in the oven. Solution: Use less sugar. Increase the oven temperature and decrease the "
[text-71] "8. This is adapted from a Cooks’ Illustrated recipe. I reduced sweetness (plus this made it a touch softer), cut out a step to brown butter (which they do to add more flavour which I don’t miss when I exclude) and I reduced the butter a touch which I find makes the dough slightly quicker to make and"
[text-72] "9. Yes, this makes 13 large cookies. It is so annoying because my trays fit 6 each! Nutrition is per giant cookie, halve it for small cookies."

[text-74] "DID YOU MAKE THIS RECIPE? I love hearing how you went with my recipes! Tag me on Instagram at @recipe_tin."

[text-76] "At the coffee shop responding to messages and recipe questions on my site…..and Dozer wanting to know what I’m writing. That’s a nice way of saying he’s being annoying, shoving his face onto my computer!!"
[text-77] "Dozer was my beautiful dog and faithful companion for 14 years. He was also official taste-tester of RecipeTin Eats, and filled every day with joy, mischief and laughs. He passed away in February 2026. I miss him every day. The Life Of Dozer section shares the happiest moments of his life and keeps "
[text-78] "IN LOVING MEMORY OF DOZER"
[text-79] "2012 – 2026"

outcome.instructions: Is what the user asked for done? First: if a pop-up, sign-in prompt or challenge covers the page now, choose in_the_way; a cookie strip or other notice on the page that covers nothing is not in the way. Otherwise judge by their words and Done so far, not by the page alone: choose yes when the page shows what they asked to see (for a question, when Text in view states its answer), or Done so far shows the action they asked for has happened; not_yet when more steps are needed.

options.yes: done: the page shows it or its answer, or the action they asked for has happened
options.in_the_way: a pop-up or prompt covers the page now
options.not_yet: not done: more to do, nothing covering the page

progress.instructions: Did the last action in Done so far bring the page closer to what the user's words ask for? Judge by what it did and the page now: closer when it did part or all of what they asked, or opened the way to it; not closer when what changed is not what they asked for.

passage.instructions: Which block of Text in view states what the user asked to know, in the page's own words? Choose none when no block states it, or when the user asked for an action and nothing to be told.
